pairs.reason: The two HttpFetchContract implementations, `_default_http_fetcher` and `_default_cffi_fetcher`, must spell the contract's parameter list identically or they are not the same contract. `test_http_fetcher_contract_holds_tree_wide` requires each to be a module-level AsyncFunctionDef in app/ whose positional names, keyword-only names, and defaulted set equal HttpFetchContract.__call__'s, and `test_the_contract_is_not_vacuous_tree_wide` requires the sweep to find exactly these two names, so neither can be a closure, a functools.partial, or a factory-produced object. The one lever that would clear the clone -- a positional-only `/` marker on one twin -- was found and rejected: it makes the twins non-interchangeable, which is the property the protocol exists to assert. This is duplication with a machine-checked guard attached, so it is the opposite of drift: the guard fails if the two ever disagree, including if either one silently gains a default that would disable the SSRF policy gate.

extract_content and _extract_html are the two entry points to one selector contract, and `_selector_contract_offenders` requires both to declare css_selector and xpath, in that order, both defaulted to None, both returning ExtractedContent -- which pins the closing annotation line too. Three identical lines are therefore mandatory, and jscpd at 4 lines reports any run of three (measured: a three-line run inside a five-line window is reported, a two-line run is not), so no spelling of this avoids the record. The fix that would remove it is building a Selectors value in content_pipeline and splatting it, which makes one declaration instead of two; that changes both call sites and the guard, so it is a deliberate change rather than a cleanup. Until then the contract is enforced and the copy is what makes it enforceable.
